properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From Field log entry 2026-10-09 (hxm_program hub, VS Code 1.140, reflow2 0.80.0). The reporter's idea, in their words: "the refusal could suggest a matching Contributor from a linked hub, or add_decision could accept approver plus a one-shot contributor record."

WHY: fact:a-member-store-refuses-an-approver-its-hub-knows-because-contributors-live-in-one-store-2026-10-09.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE REFUSAL NAMES THE MATCH: when the id exists in a design this store pins, or in one that pins it and is reachable, the refusal says so and gives the one add_contributor call. Nothing is written without the call. Cheap.
(b) A ONE-SHOT RECORD: add_decision takes approver_contributor (name, kind) and creates the Contributor in the same write. One call, but a typo creates a person.
(c) A FAMILY'S WHO-IS-WHO: members resolve a Contributor through their hub's pin, so one record serves the family. Larger. It is one piece of req:a-set-of-designs-that-make-up-one-system-is-worked-as-one-design-graph.

COUNTERPOINTS: the refusal exists so an approver is a name somebody can check (dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id). (a) keeps that, since the hub record is checkable through a declared pin. (b) weakens it. (c) moves the check to the hub, and on flo2.io the gateway already names the caller per account.



═══ KEPT AS INTENT 2026-10-09 — OPTION (A) ONLY; (B) AND (C) STAY CONSIDERED ═══
Anthony, 2026-10-09, kept this as intent when asked which of the field log's four ideas to keep (he kept all four). Promoted into req:an-approver-missing-here-but-known-to-a-pinned-design-is-named-in-the-refusal.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-09 — kept as intent, option (a) only; (b) and (c) stay considered: An approver missing from this design but known to a design it pins is named in the refusal, with the one call that records them here
